clue.text: Judge's publication is a characteristic pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the preceding words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a publication is a MAG(azine), IS stays as written, and a characteristic is a TRAIT, run together as one spoken phrase

explanation.surface: A magistrate's published ruling turns out to be a typical statement from the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Judge stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. Say MAG IS TRAIT and it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a lay or stipendiary justice who sits in a lower court, a kind of judge.

clue.text: Brass's proverbial accompaniment

parts.note: the northern English proverb 'where there's ... there's brass' pairs dirt with money, brass being slang for cash

explanation.surface: A brass band's customary backing.
explanation.definitionFit: In the proverb, dirty work and money go together, so filth is brass's companion.

clue.text: Turn to doctors in, for example, rising colour

indicators.note: the word in tells us the pieces before it are placed inside the turn

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go
to in the sense 'per', as in miles to the gallon, gives A
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the abbreviation for example is read upwards

parts.note: for example abbreviates to EG

explanation.surface: Someone turns to the doctors, perhaps because their colour is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns EG into GE in this down clue. 'to' supplying A rests on its 'per' sense, a loose equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a deep yellow pigment from a tree resin, used as a paint colour.

clue.text: Picture sequence showing shortly about tour by wagon

indicators.note: about means going round, so shortly is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: shortly means soon
a tour is a trip
a wagon is a cart

explanation.surface: A comic strip about a wagon tour, told briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the wrap, with 'showing' and 'by' as links. 'shortly' looks like it qualifies the picture sequence but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip in a newspaper is a short series of drawn panels telling a story.

clue.text: Repairs made by engineers on sidewalk

annotationWithheld.why: Repairs made by engineers on sidewalk (8): RE (engineers) is clear, but no reading of 'made by ... on sidewalk' yields MEDIES; the scan prints it this way and no source gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Repairs made by engineers on sidewalk

clue.text: Opening of tropical flower depicted in sampler

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from tropical

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: An embroidered sampler shows the bloom of a tropical flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sampler' looks like embroidery but means one who tastes; 'depicted in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster samples food or drink, so a sampler is someone who tries a little.

clue.text: Kind of party to decline without tough leader

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the decline wraps round the letter

parts.note: to decline is to sag

indicators.note: the leader of tough is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone turning down a party because no hard man is leading it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside', so SAG goes round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party is a men-only celebration before a wedding.

clue.text: Ran around in flap in storm

indicators.note: the first in tells us the rearranged letters go inside the flap

parts.note: a flap or fuss is a to-do

indicators.note: around signals the letters of ran are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone ran about in a panic during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the letters of 'Ran' before they go into the flap; only the first 'in' is an indicator, the second a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm.

clue.text: Mercenary female or male down under

definitions.meaning: a woman who courts rich men for their money
in Australia a man who prospects for ... also being Australian slang for a man

explanation.surface: A grasping woman, or an Australian man.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers both a woman chasing wealth and a man digging for the precious metal in the Australian goldfields.

clue.text: Firm undertaking to protect the Mark put at risk

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the mark goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
an undertaking is a promise
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A company pledges to shield the Deutschmark when it is in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise security or safety is to endanger it.

clue.text: Examination lesson abandoned by Head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: the lesson of a story is its moral

explanation.surface: A headteacher walks out of an exam lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the headteacher but simply means the first letter of MORAL goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken test, as in a language exam.

clue.text: Centre for display of speed in first-class dramatic setting

indicators.note: in tells us the speed abbreviation sits inside first-class

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-class
mph, miles per hour, measures speed
a theatre is where drama is staged

explanation.surface: A grand stage where speed is shown off in a top-quality theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is written with the figure 1 as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is an open circular arena where spectacles are staged.

clue.text: Army leader riding in brilliant action

parts.note: CO, commanding officer, leads an army unit
a jockey who is riding is said to be up

explanation.surface: A commander on horseback in a dazzling engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means riding, as in a racecard's 'Dettori up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a masterstroke, a notably successful move.

clue.text: State of mind?

parts.note: read literally, a 'state' or country that exists only in the head, the realm of sleep and fantasy

explanation.surface: A question about mood or mental condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamland is the imagined country one visits in sleep, a region of the mind.

clue.text: Thoroughly cured, we hear, and comfortable

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words before it are judged by their sound

parts.note: well means thoroughly and healed means cured

explanation.surface: A patient fully recovered and now feeling at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled means wealthy, financially comfortable.

clue.text: In high spirits, being promoted

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful because of a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cheerful and lifted up in rank or position.

clue.text: There's little time in Chinese society for Press

indicators.note: in tells us the short time goes inside the society

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a short stretch of time

explanation.surface: Hardly any time in Chinese society for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the media but is a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A press of people is a crowd, a crush.

clue.text: Leading supporters of Napoleon, say

parts.note: the front limbs of an animal, Napoleon being the pig in Orwell's Animal Farm, not the emperor's chief backers

explanation.surface: The emperor's foremost political allies.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's front legs bear its weight at the front, so they lead its support.

clue.text: Belloc at ease in this position

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words Belloc at ease

explanation.surface: The writer Belloc relaxing in this posture.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to position or site it.

clue.text: Toxic chemical production polluting nice day

indicators.note: polluting spoils the letters, mixing them into a new order

explanation.surface: A factory's poison emissions spoil a pleasant day.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanide is a deadly poisonous compound.

clue.text: May be drunk but easily carried when run in

indicators.note: in tells us the run letter goes inside the drinkable word

parts.note: potable means drinkable
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A drink that is fine to consume and light to carry once it's broken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable means light and handy enough to carry about.

clue.text: Lawyers with no clear title

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
O, a nought, means none
net means clear, as in net profit

explanation.surface: Lawyers without a clear claim to a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British rank below baron.

clue.text: More spirited drivers? That's right

parts.note: the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motorists' organisation
that is abbreviates to i.e.

explanation.surface: Asking whether racing drivers are livelier, and being told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Racier means livelier or more risqué.

clue.text: Possibly able to speak Polish, say

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of able may be rearranged

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone can speak the Polish language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is the verb to polish, i.e. refine, not the language.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to refine or add detail, as one polishes a draft.

clue.text: Nobleman in real trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means disturbed, so the letters of real are jumbled

explanation.surface: An aristocrat in serious difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking below a marquess.

clue.text: Stomach garments

definitions.meaning: to tolerate or put up with

explanation.surface: Clothing for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to tolerate, and clothing collectively.

clue.text: Beastly accommodation for student display

parts.note: L is for learner, a student driver
to air is to display

explanation.surface: Grim lodgings for a student exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild animal's den.

clue.text: Alighieri accepting unusual title as a lover of the Arts

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the poet's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of title are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dante taking an odd title as an arts lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' scrambles 'title', and 'accepting' sets that inside the poet's surname-like first name just after its first letter; 'as a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in the arts out of amateur enthusiasm.

clue.text: Long grass making a retreat for animals

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the grass is read in reverse

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: Tall grass providing cover for wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer are hoofed animals; the word is also plural.

clue.text: Miner perhaps in expectation soldiers on

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the soldiers come after the expectation

parts.note: a prospect is an expectation
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A hopeful miner keeps on soldiering.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector searches for minerals, so may be a miner.
